This is a read-only planning result. No Cargo, Gradle, app, compiler, SDK probe, branch, product source, fixture, canonical parity matrix, or protected branch was changed. New parity credit is **zero**. Implementation and execution remain required.

## Exact presentation behavior to port

1. `AndroidViewModuleNode.toTestString` and `update` both use `getDisplayNameForModule()`. `AndroidModuleNode.toTestString` adds ` (Android)` for a live Android module; disposed and null modules produce their distinct sentinel strings. Neither operation uses the holder-group display API.
2. `GradleModuleSystem.getDisplayNameForModule` returns the imported module name when the module is not registered as Gradle-aware. For a Gradle source-set module it delegates to `GradleProjectResolverUtil.getSourceSetName`, which takes the suffix after the final colon in the external project ID. For other Gradle modules it uses the entire external project ID when external project path equals external root project path; otherwise it uses the final colon-delimited component. It falls back to the imported module name only when the result is null.
3. `getDisplayNameForModuleGroup` instead returns the holder module's **internal imported name**. This is used by other features, including Lint/manifest source display, and is not the Android tree label API. `AndroidModuleNode.getSortKey` also uses the internal module name. A producer must retain display label, holder/group name, and sort identity separately.
4. Internal names depend on the import mode: phased sync, qualified names, root build identity, included builds, buildSrc groups, source-set names, forbidden-character escaping, and existing module-name collisions. `GradleProjectResolverUtil.resolveSourceSetModuleName` appends `~1` for an existing source-set-name collision. Root external IDs use the root project's reported name for empty/colon-only identity paths. The Gradle project path alone is insufficient to reproduce all of these inputs.
5. Null and empty are distinct. The pinned `getSourceSetName` accepts the empty suffix of an external project ID ending in `:`. The pinned display method does not replace that empty value. The current Rust adapter rejects empty or multiline display names as unavailable; this specifically applicable behavior stays **UNPORTED**, with an explicitly unsupported adapter input boundary requiring future Rust presentation-producer and adapter-extension tests. It is not N/A and must not be normalized silently.
6. Package compactness is a view preference, not a Gradle model property. Capture it with the same preference revision used for the tree, separately from import metadata.

## Exact Kotlin capability behavior to port

`AndroidViewNodeDefaultProvider` sets `kotlinEnabled` to `module.getAllLinkedModules().any { it.hasKotlinFacet() }`. `hasKotlinFacet` calls `KotlinFacet.get`; disposed modules return null. A missing linked group falls back to the module itself. A present group enumerates holder, main, unit-test, Android-test, test-fixtures, screenshot-test, and test-suite modules in that order, dropping unresolved module pointers.

The Android postprocessor configures facets for imported source-set modules. The Kotlin source-set name is the selected variant plus a capitalized non-main source-set suffix; single-module import uses the selected variant directly. `configureFacetByGradleModule` then applies these branches:

- New MPP source-set info suppresses this legacy import path; it does not prove there is no Kotlin facet supplied by the MPP importer.
- An unresolved Kotlin project model returns without creating or removing a facet. Existing facet state therefore matters during a failed/incomplete reimport.
- A missing Kotlin model or `hasKotlinPlugin == false` removes an existing facet and returns null.
- No matching Kotlin source-set data returns without creating a facet.
- A compiler version must resolve from the source-set model or Kotlin Gradle facade; unknown version prevents creation.
- After those gates, the importer creates or reuses the facet and applies platform/compiler/source-folder/friend-module settings.

The model builder treats AGP built-in Kotlin as one way to detect a Kotlin plugin, by inspecting an applied plugin interface named `org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.plugin.KotlinJvmFactory`. That input still passes through model selection, source-set matching, version resolution, and import publication before it produces a facet. SDK `useBuiltInKotlinSupport` describes a build capability; it is not the linked-group facet aggregate.

A Rust replacement should represent per-module import outcomes explicitly (`present`, `absent`, `unresolved/unsupported`), retain previous committed capability across an unresolved import only where the reference does, and aggregate only a complete, revision-bound linked group. `Enabled` can follow an authoritative present member. `Disabled` requires authoritative absence for every relevant member. If the importer cannot establish a member or the MPP alternative path is unsupported, expose `Unknown` with a reason; do not infer absence.

## Practical Rust producer boundary and exceptions

Use an additive, versioned import-facts sidecar so the existing public `Module`, `Variant`, and provider DTOs remain compatible. Its raw facts should identify the build root and identity path, root/project names, external project/root paths, Gradle-aware/type/source-set attributes, import-mode settings, existing identity collision set, selected variant, artifact-to-source-set mapping, raw Kotlin model/plugin/version/source-set metadata, and previous committed import token. Bind every result to the model/import revision and immutable file/view-preference revision already required by the adapter.

The official Gradle/AGP/KGP JVM runtime and minimal getter/serialization bridge remain a documented non-Rust exception: those evaluated model objects live inside the JVM and have no practical equivalent Rust producer. Keep the bridge limited to getting evaluated values, distinguishing absent/unavailable/null/empty, and serializing them. Root naming, module identity, source-set mapping, collision handling, Kotlin creation/removal gates, previous-state handling, linked aggregation, and presentation selection must be Rust. Hosting IntelliJ or its Kotlin importer to produce facets is not a newly approved exception and is not necessary for this proposed Rust boundary.

A public, stable KGP getter for every required compiler/source-set fact has not been proven. Add a captured unsupported capability rather than parsing build-script text or guessing from file extensions. The existing full Gradle getter bridge has no imported identity/Kotlin sidecar yet. Minimal transport feasibility needs an isolated actual SDK/KGP probe before implementation can promise an authoritative producer for supported versions. MPP requires its own authoritative import path; the legacy configure-facet branch returning null is insufficient.
